description:
Light theme token overrides: token name to value; they merge over the built-in defaults.

Example: `@use "@wovenui/core" with ($light-theme: ("brand": brand 600, "bg-base": #fff));`

groupDescriptions.config:
Theme token definitions and validation.

Theme maps are keyed by token name without the --wu- prefix ("bg-surface" is --wu-bg-surface).

A value is a color (#fff), any CSS value (2px), or a scale reference: a two-item list of scale name and stop, e.g. brand 600 or gray 200, emitted as var(--wu-brand-600).

text-on-{role} is computed from the {role} fill with find-text-color() in light and dark alike, choosing between that theme's text-regular and text-inverted, unless a theme sets text-on-{role}.

A new key must be set in both $light-theme and $dark-theme (in $light-theme alone when dark mode is off).

usedBy.description: Picks whichever of two text colors has the higher WCAG contrast against the background, by default the light theme text-regular and text-inverted; a transparent background raises an error.

description:
Applies WovenUI mixins by name in one call; each item may be followed by one state (hover, focus) and one breakpoint (sm, md, lg), which wrap it in &:state (group-hover: .group:hover &) and media-up().

Modifiers come after the mixin, state and breakpoint in either order: bg(gray, 100) hover lg or bg(gray, 100) lg hover. A modifier must be a configured breakpoint or a supported state: hover, focus, focus-visible, focus-within, active, visited, disabled, enabled, checked, required, invalid, valid, placeholder-shown, read-only, first-child, last-child, only-child, first-of-type, last-of-type, empty, target, group-hover. An unknown modifier, or more than one breakpoint or state, raises an error. Output order does not follow the written order: items without a modifier first, then state items, then each breakpoint from the smallest up with its state items; states follow the LVHA order (first-child, last-child, only-child, first-of-type, last-of-type, empty, target, visited, checked, placeholder-shown, required, valid, invalid, read-only, group-hover, focus-within, hover, focus, focus-visible, active, enabled, disabled), so flex md, hide gives the same CSS as hide, flex md and focus beats hover. Plain-text items (namespaced use) get numeric arguments as real numbers (12px, 250ms). Items of keys and words are cached; items with raw values go in a size-capped cache, so repeated raw values are parsed once and unique ones do not slow later calls.

context.name: apply
context.code: $df: (); $lr: 0; @each $mixin in $mixins { $entry: null; @if meta.type-of($mixin) == 'map' and map.has-key($mixin, _n) { $entry: (map.get($mixin, _n), map.get($mixin, _p), null, null, 0); } @else if meta.type-of($mixin) == 'list' and list.separator($mixin) == space { $first: list.nth($mixin, 1); @if meta.type-of($first) == 'map' and map.has-key($first, _n) { $pm: amo($mixin, $first, 2); $entry: (map.get($first, _n), map.get($first, _p), list.nth($pm, 1), list.nth($pm, 2), list.nth($pm, 3)); } @else { $entry: pai(#{$mixin}); } } @else { $entry: pai(#{$mixin}); } @if list.nth($entry, 1) { $rank: list.nth($entry, 5); @if $rank == 0 { @include am(list.nth($entry, 1), list.nth($entry, 2)); } @else if $rank >= $lr { $df: list.append($df, $entry, $separator: comma); $lr: $rank; } @else { $so: (); $pl: false; @each $item in $df { @if not $pl and list.nth($item, 5) > $rank { $so: list.append($so, $entry, $separator: comma); $pl: true; } $so: list.append($so, $item, $separator: comma); } $df: $so; } } } @each $item in $df { $name: list.nth($item, 1); $params: list.nth($item, 2); $bp: list.nth($item, 3); $state: list.nth($item, 4); @if not $state { @include media-up($bp) { @include am($name, $params); } } @else if $state == 'group-hover' and $bp { @include media-up($bp) { .group:hover & { @include am($name, $params); } } } @else if $state == 'group-hover' { .group:hover & { @include am($name, $params); } } @else if $bp { @include media-up($bp) { &:#{$state} { @include am($name, $params); } } } @else { &:#{$state} { @include am($name, $params); } } }

parameter.name: mixins
parameter.description: Mixin calls such as p(4), bg(brand) hover or flex md; a mixin without arguments is written bare (flex, transition)

usedBy.description:
Applies WovenUI mixins by name in one call; each item may be followed by one state (hover, focus) and one breakpoint (sm, md, lg), which wrap it in &:state (group-hover: .group:hover &) and media-up().

Modifiers come after the mixin, state and breakpoint in either order: bg(gray, 100) hover lg or bg(gray, 100) lg hover. A modifier must be a configured breakpoint or a supported state: hover, focus, focus-visible, focus-within, active, visited, disabled, enabled, checked, required, invalid, valid, placeholder-shown, read-only, first-child, last-child, only-child, first-of-type, last-of-type, empty, target, group-hover. An unknown modifier, or more than one breakpoint or state, raises an error. Output order does not follow the written order: items without a modifier first, then state items, then each breakpoint from the smallest up with its state items; states follow the LVHA order (first-child, last-child, only-child, first-of-type, last-of-type, empty, target, visited, checked, placeholder-shown, required, valid, invalid, read-only, group-hover, focus-within, hover, focus, focus-visible, active, enabled, disabled), so flex md, hide gives the same CSS as hide, flex md and focus beats hover. Plain-text items (namespaced use) get numeric arguments as real numbers (12px, 250ms). Items of keys and words are cached; items with raw values go in a size-capped cache, so repeated raw values are parsed once and unique ones do not slow later calls.

groupDescriptions.backdrop-filters:
Provides utility classes and mixins for backdrop-filter effects. All utilities come with responsive variants. Filter classes (.backdrop-blur-*, .backdrop-brightness-*, .backdrop-hue-rotate-*, etc.) only set a --wu-backdrop-* variable; .backdrop-layer writes the backdrop-filter property that combines them, so both classes are required. Presets (.backdrop-frosted, .backdrop-glass, etc.) and .backdrop-none set backdrop-filter directly and work alone. ```html
Blurred backdrop
Blurred and darkened backdrop
Blurred backdrop on medium screens and up
Preset, no layer needed
```

description: Common border styles

groupDescriptions.borders:
Border utility classes for WovenUI.

Classes:

- border, border-{t|r|b|l|s|e|x|y}: Border on all sides or one side (width 1)
- border-{0|1|2|4|8}, border-{t|r|b|l|s|e|x|y}-{width}: Border width, optionally per side
- border-{solid|dashed|dotted|double|none}: Border style

description:
Draws a border on all sides with a width key, a style and a color that defaults to the border-regular token.

A unitless width that is not a key, such as 3, raises an error; an unknown style raises an error.

context.name: border

parameter.name: val
parameter.description: A $border-widths key (0, 1, 2, 4, 8) giving var(--wu-border-width-*), or a length such as 3px

parameter.name: style
parameter.description: solid, dashed, dotted, double, none, a CSS-wide keyword or var(); written to --wu-border-style

parameter.name: color
parameter.description: A role, palette name, theme word (regular, strong, control, control-hover, focus), color value or var(); resolved like border-color()

output: border-width, border-style: var(--wu-border-style), border-color and --wu-border-style; a zero width emits border-width only

see.description:
Sets border-color from a role, palette name, theme word or color, emitting the matching var(--wu-*) token.

Roles give their fill {role} and palette names give {hue}-500; a shade outside 50 to 950 raises an error, and a raw color with a shade is shaded at compile time.

Sets --wu-border-style, which changes the style of borders drawn by border(), border-top() and the other side mixins on the same element.

Include it after the border mixin, which also writes --wu-border-style; an unknown style raises an error.

Draws a border on all sides with a width, a style and a color, all required; the same output as border() with every argument given.

The style goes through --wu-border-style, so border-style() and .border-{style} classes change it, as with border().

description:
Sets --wu-border-style, which changes the style of borders drawn by border(), border-top() and the other side mixins on the same element.

Include it after the border mixin, which also writes --wu-border-style; an unknown style raises an error.

parameter.name: style
parameter.description: solid, dashed, dotted, double, none, a CSS-wide keyword or var()

output: --wu-border-style only; it draws nothing without a border mixin or class

see.description:
Draws a border on all sides with a width key, a style and a color that defaults to the border-regular token.

A unitless width that is not a key, such as 3, raises an error; an unknown style raises an error.

description:
Sets border-color from a role, palette name, theme word or color, emitting the matching var(--wu-*) token.

Roles give their fill {role} and palette names give {hue}-500; a shade outside 50 to 950 raises an error, and a raw color with a shade is shaded at compile time.

parameter.name: color
parameter.description: A role (brand, danger), role state (danger-border, brand-hover), palette name (red), theme word (regular, strong, control, control-hover, focus), color value or var()

parameter.name: shade
parameter.description: A shade stop (50, 100 to 900, 950) for a role or palette name

see.description:
Draws a border on all sides with a width key, a style and a color that defaults to the border-regular token.

A unitless width that is not a key, such as 3, raises an error; an unknown style raises an error.

context.name: border

see.description:
Sets background-color from a role, palette name, theme word or color, emitting the matching var(--wu-*) token.

bg(brand) gives var(--wu-brand) and bg(red) the fixed var(--wu-red-500); a shade outside 50 to 950 raises an error, and a raw color with a shade is shaded at compile time.

Sets color from a role, palette name, theme word or color, emitting the matching var(--wu-text-*) token.

text-color(brand) gives var(--wu-text-brand) and text-color(red) the theme aware var(--wu-text-red); with a shade the token is var(--wu-{name}-{stop}).

description:
Sets background-color and the higher contrast text color, both computed at compile time; under prefers-contrast: more the background moves away from the text color (darker under light text, lighter under dark text) for a higher ratio.

The output is resolved color values, not var(--wu-*) tokens, so the result does not follow themes.

context.name: adaptive-contrast

parameter.name: color
parameter.description: A role or palette name (resolved with get-color()) or a color value

see.description:
Sets background-color from a role, palette name, theme word or color, emitting the matching var(--wu-*) token.

bg(brand) gives var(--wu-brand) and bg(red) the fixed var(--wu-red-500); a shade outside 50 to 950 raises an error, and a raw color with a shade is shaded at compile time.

Sets the text color for content placed on a filled color: a role gives its var(--wu-text-on-*) token, anything else the higher contrast text color computed at compile time.

A role with a shade, a palette name or a color value gives a fixed color that does not follow themes.

context.name: text-on-color

text-on-color(#{$name}): unknown color. Use a role (#{map.keys(config-color.$semantic-colors)}), a palette name (#{config-color.$primitive-color-names}) or a color value.

description:
Sets background-image to a linear-gradient with the given direction and color stops; color names resolve like bg() (roles, palette names, theme words), other colors and positions are written as passed.

An unknown color word raises the same error as bg().

parameter.name: direction
parameter.description: A direction such as to right or an angle such as 135deg

parameter.name: colors
parameter.description: Color stops: a role (brand), palette name (red), theme word (surface), color value or var(), each optionally followed by a position (brand 20%)

see.description:
Sets background-color from a role, palette name, theme word or color, emitting the matching var(--wu-*) token.

bg(brand) gives var(--wu-brand) and bg(red) the fixed var(--wu-red-500); a shade outside 50 to 950 raises an error, and a raw color with a shade is shaded at compile time.

groupDescriptions.colors: Color mixins (bg, text-color, text-on-color, gradient, adaptive-contrast) and the color name resolver shared with border-color.

description: Sets the cursor property to a CSS cursor keyword, or to a value holding a function such as url() or var(); any other word raises an error.

context.name: cursor

parameter.name: cursor-value
parameter.description: A cursor keyword (pointer, not-allowed, grab), or a value with url(), image-set() or var(), such as url(hand.svg), pointer

groupDescriptions.cursor:
Cursor utilities.

Classes:

- cursor-{value}: Sets the cursor (cursor-pointer, cursor-not-allowed, cursor-grab, cursor-wait)

The mixin also accepts url(), image-set() and var() values.

throw: cursor: unknown value #{$text}. Use a cursor keyword (#{$-cursor-keywords}), url() or var().

description: Sets display to none.

see.description: Sets display to none, exactly like hide.

groupDescriptions.display:

groupDescriptions.opacity:
Controls element transparency with customizable opacity values and interactive states. ```html
This element has 50% opacity
100% opacity by default, 50% on medium screens and up
50% opacity, becomes fully visible on hover
75% opacity, fully visible when clicked/active

Parent element with "group" class

Hidden by default, visible when parent is hovered
Smooth opacity transition on hover
``` Base: - opacity-{value}: Sets element opacity (0-100%) - Values: the $opacities keys (0, 5, 10, 20, 25, 30, 33, 40, 50, 60, 66, 70, 75, 80, 90, 100 by default) Interactive states: - hover:opacity-{value}: Changes opacity on mouse hover - focus:opacity-{value}: Changes opacity when element receives focus - active:opacity-{value}: Changes opacity when element is active/pressed - group-hover:opacity-{value}: Changes opacity when parent with .group class is hovered Animation: - transition-opacity: Adds smooth transition when opacity changes Responsive: all opacity classes support responsive variants using the @breakpoint suffix: - opacity-50@sm: 50% opacity on small screens and up - hover:opacity-100@md: Full opacity on hover for medium screens and up Available breakpoints: xs, sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl Customization: opacity values are defined in the $opacities map (config/_opacity.scss) and emitted as --wu-opacity-{key} tokens. Transition timing can be customized via CSS variables. See also the transitions utilities (utilities/_transitions.scss).

This header sticks to the top when scrolling

``` Position types: - static: Default position, follows document flow - relative: Positioned relative to normal position - absolute: Positioned relative to nearest positioned ancestor - fixed: Positioned relative to viewport - sticky: Positioned based on scroll position Inset: - inset-{key}, inset-x-{key}, inset-y-{key}: Sets inset, left and right, or top and bottom from the spacing scale - inset-auto, inset-x-auto, inset-y-auto: Resets the matching sides to auto Placement: - top-{value}: Sets top position - right-{value}: Sets right position - bottom-{value}: Sets bottom position - left-{value}: Sets left position - start-{value}, end-{value}: Sets inset-inline-start and inset-inline-end (follow text direction) Common values: spacing keys 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, etc. (var(--wu-space-*)) and fractions 25p, 33p, 50p, 66p, 75p, 100p (percentages) Responsive: all position classes support responsive variants using the @breakpoint suffix: - relative@md: Relative positioning on medium screens and up - top-0@lg: Zero top position on large screens See also z-index and transform.

These values are used to generate position utility classes like .top-25p, .left-50p, etc.

groupDescriptions.position:
Controls element positioning and placement within the document flow. ```html
Positioned in top-right corner
This header sticks to the top when scrolling
Only positioned on medium screens and up
``` Position types: - static: Default position, follows document flow - relative: Positioned relative to normal position - absolute: Positioned relative to nearest positioned ancestor - fixed: Positioned relative to viewport - sticky: Positioned based on scroll position Inset: - inset-{key}, inset-x-{key}, inset-y-{key}: Sets inset, left and right, or top and bottom from the spacing scale - inset-auto, inset-x-auto, inset-y-auto: Resets the matching sides to auto Placement: - top-{value}: Sets top position - right-{value}: Sets right position - bottom-{value}: Sets bottom position - left-{value}: Sets left position - start-{value}, end-{value}: Sets inset-inline-start and inset-inline-end (follow text direction) Common values: spacing keys 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, etc. (var(--wu-space-*)) and fractions 25p, 33p, 50p, 66p, 75p, 100p (percentages) Responsive: all position classes support responsive variants using the @breakpoint suffix: - relative@md: Relative positioning on medium screens and up - top-0@lg: Zero top position on large screens See also z-index and transform.

description: Sets box-shadow from explicit offset, blur, spread and color values.

context.name: shadow-base
context.code: box-shadow: fn-math.css-arg($x) fn-math.css-arg($y) fn-math.css-arg($blur) fn-math.css-arg($spread) fn-math.css-arg($color);

parameter.name: x
parameter.description: Horizontal offset

parameter.name: y
parameter.description: Vertical offset

parameter.name: blur
parameter.description: Blur radius

parameter.name: spread
parameter.description: Spread radius

parameter.name: color
parameter.description: Shadow color

see.description:
Sets box-shadow from a configured size; the default color emits the var(--wu-shadow-*) token when the theme feature is on, other colors emit a raw shadow.

Unknown size or color keys raise an error.

groupDescriptions.shadows:
Shadow utilities: .shadow-{size}, .shadow-{size}-{color}, .shadow-inset-{size}, .shadow-inset-{size}-{color}, .shadow-none, hover:, focus: and active: variants, and .elevation-{1-5}. Sizes and colors come from config/_shadows.scss.

Responsive variants use the @breakpoint suffix (.shadow-md@lg); active: classes have no responsive variant, and shadow-inset-* and elevation-* have no responsive or state variants.

description:

see.description:
Sets a shadow and a matching z-index for levels 1 to 5 (sm, md, lg, xl, monster); other levels raise an error.

The z-index is the level itself (1 to 5), a small local scale that orders raised siblings; it is not a $z-index-levels token. Use z-index(dropdown), z-index(modal) and the other level tokens for page layers.

see.description:
Moves the element on the x axis, and on the y axis when $y is given, then writes the combined transform.

A single argument moves the x axis only.

context.name: translate

see.description:
Rotates the element by setting --wu-rotate and writing the combined transform.

0 is written 0deg. Another unitless number, such as 30, and any other word raise an error.

groupDescriptions.transforms:
Transform utilities: translate (x, y, z), scale, rotate, skew (mixins only, no classes) and transform origin.

Each transform mixin sets its own --wu-* variable and writes one combined transform, so several transforms on an element compose.

Classes:

- translate-x-{key}/translate-y-{key}: Moves by a spacing key or a fraction key (25p, 33p, 50p, 66p, 75p, 100p); -translate-x-{key} negates
- scale-{key}/scale-x-{key}/scale-y-{key}: Scales by a factor key (0, 50, 75, 90, 95, 100, 105, 110, 125, 150)
- rotate-{key}/-rotate-{key}: Rotates by an angle key (0, 45, 90, 180, 270)
- origin-{key}: Sets transform-origin (top-left, center, bottom-right)

Interactive states: hover: and group-hover: variants exist for every class. Responsive: every class supports the @breakpoint suffix.

description: Disables transitions by setting transition-property to none.

see.description:
Sets transition-duration from a $durations key, emitted as var(--wu-duration-*), or a raw time.

A unitless number that is not a key, a negative time, or a time in another unit raises an error.

Sets transition-timing-function from a $timing-functions key, emitted as var(--wu-ease-*), or a raw timing function.

Keys win over keywords, so ease(linear) gives var(--wu-ease-linear); any other value raises an error.

Sets transition-delay from a $delays key or a raw time; delays are not tokens, so a key gives its configured time.

A unitless number that is not a key raises an error.

groupDescriptions.transitions:
Transition utilities: property, duration, easing and delay.

Classes:

- transition: Sets transition-property to all with the default duration and easing tokens ($transition-default-duration, $transition-default-ease); the defaults sit in :where(), so .duration-{time} and .ease-{type} override them in any order
- transition-{property}: Transition specific properties (none, colors, opacity, shadow, transform); colors, opacity, shadow and transform get the same :where() defaults as .transition
- duration-{time}: Set transition duration
- ease-{type}: Set transition timing function
- delay-{time}: Set transition delay

Responsive: every class supports the @breakpoint suffix.

groupDescriptions.typography:
Typography utilities: font size, weight and line height, text alignment, transform, style and decoration, word breaking, white-space and letter spacing.

Classes:

- Font Size: .text-xs, .text-sm, .text-base, etc.
- Font Weight: .font-thin, .font-normal, .font-bold, etc.
- Line Height: .leading-none, .leading-tight, .leading-normal, etc.
- Text Align: .text-left, .text-center, .text-right, .text-justify, .text-start, .text-end
- Text Transform: .uppercase, .lowercase, .capitalize, .normal-case
- Text Style: .italic, .not-italic
- Text Decoration: .underline, .line-through, .no-underline

All classes above support responsive variants with the @breakpoint suffix, except .break-* and .whitespace-*:

- .text-lg@md, .font-bold@lg, etc.
